sections.html:
The answer depends on the house's condition and your deadline. Irondequoit boomed after World War II, which means an old roof, furnace or damp basement frequently tips the choice.

Roughly 78.8% of homes are owner-occupied and the midpoint value is $182,500. On a price like that, one big repair eats a noticeable share of the proceeds. Collect a contractor quote or two before you decide. Cosmetic fixes point toward a standard listing. A big repair list, an empty or inherited property, or unpaid taxes can make an as-is sale the cheaper way out, since it ends the monthly carrying costs.

  • Agent listing: reaches the most buyers, but you pay commission, host showings and wait on a buyer's loan.
  • Selling by owner: no commission, but the marketing, negotiating and paperwork are yours.
  • As-is cash sale: few contingencies and a closing day you frequently get to choose, generally for less money.

Have every bidder commit to price, closing date, proof of funds and closing costs on paper, then calculate your true take-home from each.

sections.h2: Town or city: check your tax bill
sections.html:
Irondequoit occupies the north-central part of Monroe County, wedged between the Genesee River and Irondequoit Bay, with Lake Ontario to the north. Rochester borders it to the south and west.

The line with Rochester has quirks. A narrow ribbon of city land follows the east bank of the Genesee northward, and the upper half of Durand Eastman Park and all of Seneca Park are city property, not town property. If your mailing address says Irondequoit but the house is near those parks, look at the tax bill to learn which government taxes it. Two school districts cover the town: West Irondequoit and East Irondequoit.

The town has about 50,200 residents, down 1.7% from the 2020 base. People 65 and over are 22.6% of the population, and estate sales are one reason houses come to market. Nearly 92% of residents were in the same home a year earlier, so listings are not plentiful, and a tidy house priced sensibly gets attention fast.

sections.h2: When are Irondequoit property taxes due?
sections.html:
Irondequoit homeowners get two tax bills a year from the Tax Office, which the Receiver of Taxes runs. Town and County tax arrives in late December and must be paid by February 10. School tax arrives in late August and must be paid by October 1.

Closed on the due date? Payment is accepted the next business day. A bill that never reached you does not erase the tax, and penalties cannot be waived by the office. Owners who pay directly rather than through escrow who have no bill a week after mailing should call 585-336-6050 for a duplicate. Monroe County's website displays bills as well.

For a parcel lookup, go to the county's Real Property Portal, accept its disclaimer, enter your street address and choose the Pay Property Taxes icon. School and combined town and county statements appear there with the payment history. Print the current pair for your closing attorney.

The town's tax year turns on eight dates, and a pending sale holds none of them back. Schedule your listing with them in mind.

  • March 1: taxable status date, and the last day to file new or renewal exemption applications.
  • May 1: the tentative roll goes public; a paper copy sits at Town Hall.
  • Third Tuesday in May: school budget vote.
  • Fourth Tuesday in May: Grievance Day.
  • July 1: final roll and valuation date. You have 30 days after it to ask for a judicial review (SCAR hearing).
  • Early September and early January: school bills and Town and County bills go out.

The final roll sets the figures for the next school and Town and County bills, which means a summer buyer inherits it. Review it before choosing an asking price.

File with the Assessor's Office any time from May 1 through Grievance Day, which is the fourth Tuesday of May. The next is May 25, 2027. You must go through this town step before a small claims review is available.

Bring Form RP-524 as one original and four copies, and attach backup documents for every board member. A hearing needs an appointment, and the paperwork has been due a week in advance. The assessor's tentative value is presumed right, so the proof falls on you. Recent appraisals, purchase contracts, comparable sales lists and a broker's written value opinion all count as credible evidence. Your tax bill does not count as proof of value.

The assessor may propose a stipulation before the hearing. You can decline it; if you accept, the assessed value is locked at the agreed number. If you still disagree with the board, a Small Claims Assessment Review in Monroe County Supreme Court is the next step, filed under Section 730 of the Real Property Tax Law for $30. The town also holds informal review appointments in the spring and keeps a comparable sales book of recent sales for owners to study.

sections.h2: Transfer tax and filing the deed
sections.html:
New York charges sellers $2 for every $500 of the price, though a contract can move that cost. Form TP-584 reports the tax. Residential prices of $1 million or more bring a further 1% charge for the buyer.

The Monroe County Clerk records Irondequoit deeds at 39 W. Main Street, Room 101, Rochester, NY 14614. Your closing attorney or title company usually drops them off. Your part is to sign where shown and keep copies of every page, since lenders and future buyers sometimes ask for them years later.

sections.h2: Checklist before accepting a direct offer
sections.html:
Add up your net after every cost, then check the calendar. A higher listing price can lose its edge to commission, repairs and months of mortgage, tax and utility bills.

  • Make the buyer commit in writing to who covers transfer tax and closing costs.
  • Ask for proof of funds and a fixed closing day.
  • Print the Monroe County portal statements so unpaid tax gets cleared at closing.
  • Ask a local agent for a listing-price opinion to use as a yardstick.
  • Let your own attorney go through the contract first.

A cash sale has no lender approval and no appraisal, the two steps that most often stall a financed closing. There are no showings or open houses either, so the house can stay as is while you pack. When taxes are owed, the closing attorney pays them out of your proceeds at the table, which is why current statements help.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Irondequoit?
faqs.a: Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday of May, which makes May 25, 2027 the next one. You can file from May 1 until then, and a hearing requires an appointment.

faqs.q: When are Irondequoit property taxes due?
faqs.a: Town and County tax is due February 10, School tax October 1. If the office is closed that day, the next business day works with no penalty.

faqs.q: How much does a small claims assessment review cost in Irondequoit?
faqs.a: The fee is $30 under Section 730 of the Real Property Tax Law, and Monroe County Supreme Court hears it. The town grievance has to come first.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when an Irondequoit house sells?
faqs.a: Sellers pay $2 per $500 unless the contract says otherwise. Buyers pay an added 1% when a residential sale hits $1 million.

faqs.q: Is Seneca Park part of Irondequoit?
faqs.a: No. Seneca Park and the northern half of Durand Eastman Park belong to the City of Rochester. If your house is near them, check which municipality taxes it.
